name: Intralesional cortisone injection

card.summary: A dermatologist-administered steroid shot into an inflamed cyst, discussed online as an overnight shrinker; evidence is not detailed in the sources reviewed.
card.aka: Cortisone shot for pimples, steroid cyst injection
card.note: Clinician-administered procedure; reported to be able to affect the skin locally and glucocorticoids can worsen acne.

quick.overview:
An intralesional cortisone injection is a clinic procedure where a corticosteroid is injected straight into an inflamed acne cyst or nodule. People in looksmaxxing and skincare circles discuss it as a fast way to reduce a large lesion.

Wikipedia describes it as providing immediate relief for inflamed acne lesions.
quick.mechanism: The corticosteroid is delivered into the lesion, where its anti-inflammatory glucocorticoid action is directed at the inflamed tissue.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed give little detail on side effects. Glucocorticoids are noted to be able to worsen acne in general, and the procedure is performed by clinicians.

lead: An intralesional cortisone injection is a procedure in which a clinician injects a corticosteroid directly into an inflamed lesion, such as a large, painful acne nodule. In appearance-focused communities it is discussed as a way to flatten a big pimple quickly, often described as shrinking it "overnight", for example before an event or photographs.

Wikipedia's acne article lists injection of a corticosteroid into inflamed lesions among the procedural treatments for acne [1]. It describes the deep, painful bumps of severe acne as nodules, notes that large nodules were previously called cysts, and says true cysts are rare in people with acne [1]. Triamcinolone acetonide, a synthetic glucocorticoid about five times as potent as cortisol, is one corticosteroid injected into skin lesions, with documented intralesional use for hypertrophic and keloid scars [2][3].

Inflamed acne can leave scars, which Wikipedia says are estimated to affect 95 percent of people with acne vulgaris, with atrophic scars the most common at about 75 percent of cases [1]. Reducing a lesion's inflammation is therefore of interest for both the short-term look of the skin and the long-term texture. Reports of side effects at the injection site, including a 2026 case report of facial lipoatrophy following intralesional steroid injections for papulopustular acne, are part of the literature [4].

chain: Corticosteroid is injected into an inflamed lesion
Local anti-inflammatory action reduces swelling and redness
Large pimple flattens, usually faster than untreated
angle.text: The shot delivers an anti-inflammatory steroid straight into a swollen acne nodule, which people discuss as a way to bring down a prominent blemish quickly. It is done in a clinic by a clinician.

infobox: Inflamed acne lesions [1]; keloids and hypertrophic scars [2][3]
About five times cortisol as a glucocorticoid [2]

paras: The procedure delivers a corticosteroid into the lesion itself rather than onto the skin surface or through the bloodstream. For acne, Wikipedia places it under procedural treatments alongside comedo extraction, and states it is intended for inflamed lesions [1].

Triamcinolone acetonide is described as a glucocorticoid roughly five times as potent as cortisol with very little mineralocorticoid activity, and its injection into scars is a recognised use [2]. Brand names include Kenalog [2].

Intralesional triamcinolone was introduced as a keloid treatment in the mid-1960s, according to Wikipedia's keloid article, which says it appears to reduce fibroblast activity, inflammation and itching [3]. The same article cites a 2022 Cochrane review that found only two small studies, with 36 participants in total, comparing triamcinolone with other options, and the authors could not say whether it was the most effective [3].

A 2026 case report described a 26-year-old with left-cheek atrophy that followed intralesional steroid injections given for papulopustular acne; it was treated with a multimodal protocol over about 18 months, with post-acne scarring improving from Goodman and Baron grade 3 to grade 2. The authors state that a single case does not support conclusions about effectiveness or generalisability [4].

Wikipedia notes more generally that glucocorticoid medications can worsen existing acne [1] and that triamcinolone can have endocrine effects such as ovulation inhibition and menstrual irregularities [2]. Because the procedure is performed by clinicians, agent selection and technique are matters of medical practice.
No studies found that are specific to this use in the sources consulted. The scar-treatment literature on intralesional triamcinolone is summarised above [3].

timeline.event: Intralesional triamcinolone introduced as a keloid treatment (mid-1960s) [3].
